{{Youmay|the ship dubbed ''Hieroglyph''|the [[Writing/Legends|writing system]] known as [[hieroglyphics]]}}
{{Quote|I rather like our new accomodations, myself. Comfy chairs, greel-wood paneling, and a galley section to kill for. We've always dreamed of making a big heist. Well, my friends, this is it.|Cecil Noone admiring his new vessel|<ref name="AJ15" />}}
The '''''Asaari Wind''''' was a [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub]] [[Personal Luxury Yacht 3000/Legends|Personal Luxury Yacht 3000]] owned by the Bimm [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Ritinki]] around [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]. The vessel was heavily modified by the Bimm, and featured luxurious appointments and offensive capabilities far in excess of its original specifications.

During a summit held by Ritinki and the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] kingpin [[Vop]] on the [[Ithorian Herdship]] ''[[Song of the Clouds]]'', the ''Asaari Wind'' was commandeered by the [[Thief/Legends|thief]] [[Cecil Noone]] and his [[Cecil Noone's crew|partners-in-crime]], with Ritinki being [[Death/Legends|killed]] in the course of the theft. Under Noone's ownership, the [[Yacht/Legends|yacht]] operated under the aliases '''''Hieroglyph''''', '''''Spiraling Shape''''', '''''Tailchaser''''', and '''''Voona's Dream II'''''. The vessel sustained severe damage amid the crew's frantic escape from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kabal/Legends|Kabal]] after Noone's dealings with the [[Krish/Legends|Krish]] business magnate [[Tyro Viveca/Legends|Tyro Viveca]] went awry.

==Description==
The ''Asaari Wind'' was a [[Personal Luxury Yacht 3000/Legends|Personal Luxury Yacht 3000]] manufactured by the [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]]. While in the ownership of the Bimm [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Ritinki]], the ''Asaari Wind'' had been modified. Its armaments included two light [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] and two medium [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]], all of which were linked and front-mounted and could be fired from the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], and twin heavy laser cannon turrets, as well as a rear-facing [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] mounted in place of the external observation platform typical of most [[Yacht/Legends|yachts]].<ref name="AJ15" />

The ''Asaari Wind'' could reach sublight speeds of 1,000 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] per hour, and was equipped with [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]] and [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]], as well as primary and secondary [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]]. The latter, and the yacht's standard [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]]s and [[Ion engine/Legends|ion engines]], were replaced with components used in much larger ships, including state-of-the-art [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]] drives. A [[slave circuit]] paired with a [[Beckon call/Legends|beckoncall]] transmitter enabled Ritinki to summon the ''Asaari Wind'' remotely; having been designed exclusively for Ritinki by a moonlighting [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]], the transmitter activated the yacht's engines and used the ignition command as a homing signal, which guided the ship to the Bimm's location. Measuring fifty [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length, the ''Asaari Wind'' could carry seventy [[Metric ton/Legends|metric tons]] of cargo, and accomodated two crewmembers and three gunners for basic operations, with a skeleton complement of between one and ten. The yacht also had capacity for ten passengers, and toted a [[Standard month|month]]'s worth of consumables.<ref name="AJ15" />

Though it was rugged and heavily armed, the yacht's more luxurious features were kept. Each of its five cabins was decked out with double bunks and soft [[glow-lamp]]s, and the interior spaces&mdash;save for the bridge and galley&mdash;were paneled with exotic [[Greel wood/Legends|greel-wood]]. The galley was equipped with a [[Gourmet Master 500/Legends|Gourmet Master 500]] and capacious fresh [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] storage, while the upper deck boasted an observation lounge with comfortable [[Couch/Legends|couches]] and a [[jet-stream meditation pool]]. Despite the presence of the turbolaser turret, the lounge nonetheless offered its occupants impressive views of [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]] and [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]].<ref name="AJ15" />

==History==
===Hijacking on the herdship===
{{Quote|Let's see. If I were a wealthy, underhanded Bimm with a ruthless streak and a taste for expensive starships, where would I put it?|Dawson searching the ''Asaari Wind'' for treasure|<ref name="AJ15" />}}
[[File:Cecil Noone.png|thumb|right|200px|Cecil Noone (pictured) and his crew stole the ''Asaari Wind'' in 0 ABY.]]
The ''Asaari Wind'' was purchased by the Bimm crimelord Ritinki as soon as it left the [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]], on account of Ritinki desiring a vessel free of undue modifications or [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking devices]]. The Bimm subjected the yacht to a variety of embellishments, essentially converting it into an unusual combination of pleasure craft and small combat starship with abilities far in excess of its original specifications. Even so, Ritinki took measures to ensure the vessel's systems would not be overloaded by its enhancements, though he was also intent on preserving its luxurious accoutrements.<ref name="AJ15" />

Around [[0 ABY]],<ref name="EssReaComp">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Ritinki traveled aboard the ''Asaari Wind'' to the [[Ithorian Herdship|Ithorian herdship]] ''[[Song of the Clouds]]'' over<ref name="AJ15" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] to meet with [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] kingpin [[Vop]]. Aware that Vop aimed to use the meeting to acquire a [[lockbox]] with valuable contents, Ritinki had the Rodian's [[Lyle Lippstroot|bookkeeper]] [[Death/Legends|killed]] and used a doppelganger to acquire the lockbox and secure it aboard the ''Asaari Wind''.<ref name="AJ15" />

Meanwhile, the [[Thief/Legends|thief]] [[Cecil Noone]] and his [[Cecil Noone's crew|crew]] had also infiltrated the Herdship on the orders of [[Guttu]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] to [[Heist on the Song of the Clouds|retrieve]] the lockbox. Noone's subordinates [[Dawson (Tynnan)|Dawson]] and [[Hass Sonax]], having fruitlessly scoured the Herdship for the treasure, triangulated its location to the ''Asaari Wind'' and boarded the yacht. As the meeting descended into chaos, Ritinki summoned the ''Asaari Wind'' using his beckoncall, powering it up; however, Dawson and Sonax took control of the yacht and turned its weapon systems on Ritinki as he attempted to board and escape. Noone's posse fled the herdship aboard the ''Asaari Wind'', abandoning their own ship, the ''[[Borogove]]'', in the process;<ref name="AJ15" /> Ritinki died at the scene.<ref name="Fair Prey" />

===Here, there, and everywhere===
{{Quote|Gah! We didn't get rid of that yet?|Dawson on the yacht's latest bouquet|<ref name="Fair Prey" />}}
[[File:GunofCommand2-FF76.png|thumb|left|200px|A Hapan Gun of Command (pictured) was secreted aboard the ''Asaari Wind''.]]
Over the course of the next [[Standard month|month]], the yacht went through the aliases ''Hieroglyph'', ''Tailchaser'', and ''Voona's Dream II''. During that [[Time/Legends|time]], Noone's crew attempted to sell the contents of the lockbox&mdash;a [[Hapan]] [[Gun of Command]]&mdash;to representatives of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The latter meeting took place on [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]], with<ref name="Fair Prey" /> the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="KothWhere">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Kothlis system/Legends|Kothlis system]]</ref> world's pungent atmosphere leaving the yacht's air supply system thick with the smell of putrefying [[groat cheese]].<ref name="Fair Prey" />

After both deals proved fruitless, [[Krish/Legends|Krish]] business magnate [[Tyro Viveca/Legends|Tyro Viveca]] indicated an interest in the Gun, and Noone's crew traveled aboard the yacht to<ref name="Fair Prey" /> the Outer Rim<ref name="KabalWhere">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Kabal system/Legends|Kabal system]]</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kabal/Legends|Kabal]], docking at the coastal settlement of [[Palisade]] under the alias ''Spiraling Shape''. While Noone met with Viveca, the others remained at the ship to wait for him; however, Viveca had taken to [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]] Noone on his private [[Tyro Viveca's estate|estate]], and the crew mobilized to rescue him. After defeating Viveca and retrieving Noone, the group made an escape. Though the [[landing shackle]] remained affixed to the ''Spiraling Shape'', the yacht was able to lift off and leave Kabal, albeit with severe damage as the shackle ripped two landing struts, a structural girder, several hull plates, and the aft repulsorlift assembly loose.<ref name="Fair Prey" />

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Asaari Wind'' first appeared in "[[The Great Herdship Heist]]", a short story written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and featured in the [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 15|fifteenth issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' in [[November]] [[1997]]. The illustration of the vessel was drawn by [[Will Warren]].<ref name="AJ15" />
